the sensitivity of protein crystals to radiation damage is very dependent on the structure of the protein.
the sensitivity of crystals to X-ray damage depends on the type of protein, and the presence of a solvent, and is not dependent on the type of crystal lattice or the size of the unit cell.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

The main takeaway from our work is that
radiation damage is a very complex process and cannot be described by a single decay law.
radiation damage to protein crystals at room temperature is a function of the protein crystallographer’s experimental setup and not of the protein structure itself.
